ELUCIDATION
OF

NUMBER 14 OF 2020
CONCERNING
EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates Regional Governments to regulate and manage their own regions for the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has also mandated in Article 28D Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, protection, and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution also states that every child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that women should be protected by the state, particularly against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Protection carried out by the Government towards women is concretely implemented, namely by the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.

The government's efforts in protecting its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, protection and fair legal treatment as well as to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".

Violence and trafficking against women are already regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Human Trafficking.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women, particularly for the Temanggung Regency area. The Government of Temanggung Regency is one of the most authorized parties in carrying out women's empowerment in order to provide guarantees for justice and gender equality, through efforts to build commitment to integrate gender responsive budgets in programs and activities.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage improvement efforts on access, control, participation and benefits for justice and gender equality as well as the physical and mental conditions of women victims of violence.

EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
The Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates Regional Governments to regulate and manage their own regions for the realization of community welfare through improvement of services, empowerment and community participation. One of the authorities of Regional Government is to make a regional policy with the aim of improving the welfare of the community in its region.

In addition, the constitution of the Republic of Indonesia has also mandated in Article 28D Paragraph (1) of the 1945 Constitution that every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, protection, and fair legal certainty as well as equal treatment before the law. Article 28B Paragraph (2) of the 1945 Constitution also states that every child has the right to survival, growth and development and has the right to protection from violence and discrimination. This shows that women should be protected by the state, particularly against violence because their rights are already regulated in the constitution.

Protection carried out by the Government towards women is concretely implemented, namely by the issuance of Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, hereinafter abbreviated as CEDAW.

The government's efforts in protecting its citizens, especially women, are also clearly implied in the provisions of Article 3 paragraph (2) of Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights which states that: "every person has the right to recognition, guarantee, protection and fair legal treatment as well as to obtain legal certainty and equal treatment before the law".

Violence and trafficking against women are already regulated in Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, and Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Human Trafficking.

Therefore, it is necessary to make efforts to prevent and eradicate all forms of discrimination and violence against women, particularly for the Temanggung Regency area. The Government of Temanggung Regency is one of the most authorized parties in carrying out women's empowerment in order to provide guarantees for justice and gender equality, through efforts to build commitment to integrate gender responsive budgets in programs and activities.

This Regional Regulation is expected to be able to encourage improvement efforts on access, control, participation and benefits for justice and gender equality as well as the physical and mental conditions of women victims of violence.

CHAPTER VII
PROTECTION OF WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
Part One
General

Article 34
(1) Forms of Violence against Women include:
a. physical violence;
b. sexual violence;
c. economic violence; and
d. psychological violence.
(2) The form of physical violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, unconsciousness and or causes death.
(3) The form of sexual violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, is sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.
(4) The form of economic violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, is the neglect of women in the form of not providing proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
(5) The form of psychological violence as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d, is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

10. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering in a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes or certain purposes.
12. 13. Victim is a woman including Female Workers who work abroad and children who experience suffering and/or hardship either directly or indirectly as a result of such violence.

15. 18. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group hereinafter abbreviated as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of Gender Mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by respect for Human Rights is respecting and upholding human rights law.
Letter b What is meant by Gender Equality is equal conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, legal, economic, social and cultural activities, Education and national defense and security, as well as equality in enjoying the results of such development.
Letter c What is meant by Gender Justice is a process and fair treatment of women and men. With gender justice it means there is no stereotyping of roles, double burden, subordination, marginalization and violence against women or men.

Article 19
(1) Women have the right to obtain special Protection from matters that threaten their safety and/or health.

6.8.rationale: The Indonesian text provides protections specifically connected to legal processes for victims/witnesses. Pasal 37 includes: fast handling for “saksi dan/atau Korban,” free of charge, confidentiality, guaranteeing justice/legal certainty, and “penyediaan ruang pelayanan khusus di Kantor Kepolisian.” Pasal 36 ayat (3) also defines legal protection as services/assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes (“membantu Korban dalam menjalani proses hukum dan peradilan”). So the document does address protection for women involved in legal processes; the judge’s ‘Yes’ is supported. The golden ‘No’ appears wrong.

7.2.evaluator_rationale: None of the provided passages explicitly identify the national government budget (e.g., APBN) as a funding/budget source; references to ministries and coordination do not specify national budget financing.
